hypothesis_tested: That the 20,000-row scoring batch set the memory floor, so shrinking it would raise the reachable context. Cutting the batch fourfold moved peak allocation by 1.095 GB, or 8.8%. The hypothesis is refused.
what_it_means: A context row and a scored row cost the same, to within 2.5%: 73 KB each. TabICL holds both in one attention buffer, so there is one row budget rather than two. On a T4 that budget is about 114,000 rows shared between the context and the batch being scored.
cost_of_chunking: Scoring in chunks keeps memory at the small-batch level but re-processes the context each time. At a 50,000-row context, four chunks of 5,000 cost about 248 s against 76 s for one pass of 20,000. Time is not the binding resource here, so this is an available trade.

tabpfn_run_is_partial.why: The Colab runtime reported repeated disconnects during the sweep and it was cut off after the 10,000-row configuration. The three completed rows survive because the probe now writes each row as it is measured.
tabpfn_run_is_partial.what_this_costs: TabPFN's memory is flat over the measured range, which is consistent with internal chunking but is only three points at small contexts. Whether it stays flat at 50,000 and beyond decides whether TabPFN is memory-bound at all, and it is unmeasured.
tabpfn_run_is_partial.what_survives: Peak allocation comes from a device-side counter that a frontend disconnect does not touch, and the timing spreads run from 0.18% to 4%, so the rows are internally consistent. They are treated as sound within their range and not extrapolated past it.
tabpfn_run_is_partial.superseded_by: probe-tabpfn-ceiling.json, which reached 20,000 and 50,000 rows of context at a 5,000-row scoring batch. The 100,000-row configuration was requested and has not returned.

tabpfn_vs_tabicl_at_10k_context_20k_scor.note: TabPFN buys its memory with time at this shape. The comparison is one shape on one card and is not a general claim about either model.

correction.what_was_said: That TabPFN's memory is nearly flat across context, which looked like internal chunking.
correction.what_the_wider_range_shows: It is not flat. The slope is 0.0036 GB per thousand context rows between 1,000 and 10,000, and 0.0114 between 20,000 and 50,000 - 3.2 times steeper. A linear fit over all five points leaves a 0.034 GB residual, so the growth is not linear either and extrapolation past 50,000 rows is an estimate rather than a reading.

tabicl.note: One shared row budget of about 114,000. Time is cheap.

tabpfn.note: A tenth of the card at a context TabICL cannot reach, but the seconds grow as context to the power 1.63. At 100,000 rows a single pass is around five minutes, and 87 passes is about eight hours of quota.

the_two_models_are_bound_by_different_re.consequence: There is no single row ceiling for 'the foundation models'. Each stops for its own reason in its own place, and a study design that caps them together has to say which constraint it is respecting.
the_two_models_are_bound_by_different_re.practical_operating_point: A 50,000-row context runs both: 76 s for TabICL and 106 s for TabPFN, so 87 passes is under two hours each.

how_far_these_numbers_can_be_trusted.conditions: The Colab frontend reported repeated disconnects and several sweeps were cut short. That is a property of the session, not of any individual measurement, and the two have to be separated.
how_far_these_numbers_can_be_trusted.peak_memory: Trustworthy. It comes from a device-side counter read inside the kernel process. A frontend losing its socket does not touch it.
how_far_these_numbers_can_be_trusted.timings_within_a_session: Trustworthy. Repeat spreads run from 0.16% to 3%, and the two tightest, 0.16% and 0.50%, came from the sessions that were disconnecting. An erratically throttled machine does not produce repeats that agree to a part in six hundred.
how_far_these_numbers_can_be_trusted.timings_across_sessions: Good to about 6%. The one configuration measured in two sessions - TabICL at 10,000 context and 20,000 scored - gave 13.002 s and 12.193 s. Seconds from different sessions are not comparable past that, and are not quoted to three figures here.
how_far_these_numbers_can_be_trusted.rows_that_never_printed: Do not exist and are not inferred. The probe writes each row after measuring it, so a row is either complete with its own spread or absent. There is no partially measured row.
how_far_these_numbers_can_be_trusted.does_this_threaten_the_conclusions: No. The narrowest margin any conclusion rests on is 1.4x, between 106 s and 76 s at a 50,000-row context, and that comparison is within-session on both sides. The memory findings carry margins of ten times and more. What 6% does forbid is quoting the seconds as precise, and the two time exponents rest on two points each and are indicative rather than established.
